change: Bound the dev /api/runtime.js source load and reach the existing dist fallback

defect.was: The middleware awaited loadRuntimeSourceForDev (server.ssrLoadModule) with no bound. The dist fallback was guarded by `if (!runtimeSource ...)`, which is only reachable when the load RETURNS nothing - never when it fails to return at all.
defect.consequence: A stalled load produced no HTTP response. The preview iframe never fired load, so the editor sat at timelinePhase 'load-pending' for the whole 60s mount wait, and the endpoint stayed wedged for every later request until the server was restarted.

behaviour: Source is still preferred and still re-read per request, so runtime edits remain visible; Vite's module graph stays the only cache.
A single request waits at most RUNTIME_SOURCE_TIMEOUT_MS (10000) for the source build, then serves packages/core/dist/hyperframe.runtime.iife.js and logs why.
Concurrent requests share one in-flight build instead of each starting another stuck load.
A rejected build is not remembered, so one transient failure is not replayed to later requests.
A stalled build that later settles is used again from then on.

notEstablished: The trigger for the original stall. Two attempts to reproduce it deliberately both PASSED: a cold-restarted server with a reused fixture (1957ms) and a cleared Vite dep-optimizer cache (1860ms). The captured failure's app shell was in fact FASTER than the passing runs', so contention and cold-cache cost are both ruled out as the explanation.
That this fix eliminates the AFM-059 startup failure. It removes the unbounded hang and guarantees a response; it does not explain why ssrLoadModule stalled.
Whether a dist fallback served during a real stall would be stale enough to change preview behaviour.
